What I learned in NBA last night

1) Giannis putting up 35.6 points, 17 rebounds & 15 assists per 100 possessions in preseason so far. Possible career year ahead. Will be more motivated than any year since his title. Moved to +1000 for MVP last 2 days. 

2) Cade Cunningham controlled the game against the Timberwolves after a slow start. Still only 25 years old & somehow being overlooked. Pistons won’t win 60 games in a crowded east, but John Collins & Isaiah Joe give them scalable scoring depth. 

3) Pelicans guard Jeremiah Fears will have a great 2nd season. He turned 20 years old yesterday & has future all-star tools. Knocking down 54% of his threes in preseason. Averaged 37 ppg in his final 3 games last season. He’s +8000 for most improved player & +10000 for 6th man. 

4) Jonathan Kuminga gives this Timberwolves rotation 5 legit scoring options. His team friendly contract will be one of the league’s best if he stays healthy. One of the sneakiest pickups of the entire offseason. 

5) The Celtics will have one of the best defensive frontcourts in the league with Mitchell Robinson & reserve Neemias Queta. Will be a nightmare for opposing teams. Joe Mazzulla experimented with a double big lineup with them late last night, looked promising. 

6) Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. was solid in his preseason debut against the Heat. He has a truly dynamic skillset that translates to the pro game. Had durability issues, but he’ll have every opportunity to accelerate his development with the Nets. He’s +4000 for rookie of the year.

posts.author: "Thunder Dan" Palyo
posts.text:
Preseason NBA Notes: Wed 10/14

7 Games...Going to try to hit some players I haven't talked about as much and skip obvious stuff!

PELS
They played everyone (except Dejounte, who sat) 20 min or less and brought some starters off the bench. Fears had 16 pts and 5 ast - I think his best bet for production is actually off the bench in a 25 min role. Missi went for 6 and 9 with 4 blocks and is a nice pick late in drafts if you need blocks. This team could be maddening all season.

MAVS
They might be just as frustrating. We aren't drafting anyone here other than Kyrie and Flagg with any confidence. Moussa Cisse had 8 and 6 with 4 stocks and is a guy to watch if he gets minutes this year. We know Daniel Gafford is made of glass, Aldama is hurt, and Lively is still a ways off from returning.

BULLS
Starters all did their thing, but it's worth mentioning Jalen Smith started again and had 15 points, 7 boards, three treys and a block. We know what he can do with starter minutes, and he should be getting drafted in 12-team leagues.
The Lenny Miller breakout continues as he had 18 points in 18 min off the bench. With Claxton out to start the year, he has a real chance to play decent minutes out of the gate. Tre Jones had 7 assists and is the only other bench guy I'm interested in (very late in drafts) for efficient assists.

BUCKS
Played all young guys...Burries had a nice line (19-5-5, 4 steals, 8-8 FT) and is going to be a very good player. I don't think the minutes will be there to start the year, but he's a stash guy in deep leagues or someone to add to your watch list in 12-team leagues. Ousmane Dieng went 10-11-4 with a block, while Jaku had 18 pts and 6 assists. All three guys are late-season sleepers, but that's about it.

PISTONS
Pretty normal rotation, other than the starters being done early. Isiah Joe had 14 pts off the bench, and Paul Reed went 7-3-2 with 3 stocks in 16 min. I had a draft last night where I forgot about Reed until someone took him right ahead of me because he was buried in the default ranks. He does enough with his minutes to be the last guy on your bench in a standard league.

WOLVES
Much better night for Kuminga (16-4-3 on 5-for-6 from the floor, 2 threes), but I still don't really trust em. Joan Beringer had 10 and 7 with 2 stocks. Like Reed, he's good enough per minute in a backup center role to be rosterable.

SUNS
The only rotation guys who started were Maluach and Kennard, and both played like 12 minutes. Jamaree Bouyea went for 15 and 8 assists, but he's still behind Kennard and Gillespie for guard minutes off the bench. Not much to see here.

SPURS
We got the 3-guard lineup with Fox/Harper/Castle all starting with Vassell and Wemby. Who knows if they really do this, but Wemby's rim protection allows them to play small elsewhere. Castle was the most productive with 18 points, 14 of those coming at the free-throw line, and he missed only one FT (notable as FT% is one of his flaws). Harper shot poorly (4-11) by his standards, but his 6 boards in 22 minutes are a good reminder of how strong he is on the glass.
Carter Bryant and Tarris Reed Jr. had good games off the bench, but Tobias Harris, Keldon Johnson, Luke Kornet, and Champagnie were all out.

NETS
We finally got a good Egor game (17-3-3, 4 threes) and a very solid Day'Ron line (11-6-4, 3 stocks). Keon Ellis started ahead of Mikel Brown Jr., but shot 0-7. MBJ made his preseason debut and went 15-3-3 with 2 steals. I think he'll start eventually and is the guy to roster. Nolan Traore was solid, too, but I think Egor and MBJ are going to get more minutes.

HEAT
Bam was out, so Nick Richards started at center. Giannis went off for 20-15-9 and was +15 in +/-.
Klay Thompson started at the 2, but Pelle Larsson was out. I'm still team Larsson over guys like Klay and THJ, unless you need threes.

HORNETS
Brandon Miller started 0-for-7 from the field in the first quarter, but still managed to finish with 16 pts, 3 threes, and a perfect 5-for-5 at the charity stripe. He's going to have to do a lot of heavy lifting for Charlotte early in the year with Kon/Coby out.
Saluan and rookie Christian Anderson led the team in bench minutes (21) and had solid nights. Grayson Allen was out, so he'll probably start ahead of Royce O'Neale when he comes back, with O'Neale, Salaun, Anderson, McNeeley, and Kalk being the second group. Any value from those guys is temporary, as White and Kon will eventually shift Allen and Schroder to the bench.

CELTICS
Tatum was great, Derrick White was excellent (he's a unicorn!), and Mitch Rob had a tidy 12 and 7 with 3 blocks in 17 minutes. Queta played really well, too, scoring 16 points. He's probably the starter, but both guys are going to limit each other's upside.
Pritchard had 11 assists off the bench in 29 minutes, just a reminder that he's probably the only guy available after pick 75 who can do that somewhat regularly!

NUGGETS
The starters played only about a quarter and a half. Denver played a bunch of guys, with rookie Trevon Brazile leading the team in pts (22) and minutes (25). Cam Whitmore had 17 points, but both of these performances were a product of garbage-time fourth-quarter stats. Brazile is a solid dynasty asset, but there's really nothing else notable here.

CLIPPERS
Garland and Hach were fine; Wagler started at the 2 and went 12-5-4. I'm not sure he starts day one, but I think he'll get there eventually. Stash. DJJ started at the 3, and I-Jax at the 5. Both guys are last-round dart throws. 
Baba Miller had 15-5-2 and played the most minutes off the bench. The Clips are thin with Beal, Ingram, Miller, and Strus all hurt to start the year, so he could play some right away. Stay tuned.

NBA Preseason Notes: Tuesday Night (10/13)

RAPTORS
The Toronto starters had their way with the Knicks' backups. Kawhi had an efficient 21 points; Barnes went 19-6-4 and Barrett 17-4-3.
Everyone's fave sleeper CMB went 19-9-2 and didn't miss a shot, hitting both of his three-point attempts. HOW HIGH CAN HE GO IN DRAFTS?

KNICKS
The Knicks sat all their starters and Clarkson, Drummond, and Shamet, too. So basically, just McBride, Bruce Brown, and Alvarado were the only relevant guys who played. Moving on...

BLAZERS
Scoot Henderson started next to Dame, over Morant. Probably not going to happen next week, but staggering Dame and Morant is probably a good idea when they can.
Deni had 26 points, 9 boards, and 4 assists. The consensus is that he can't repeat last year with all these guards hogging shots and taking assists, but...maybe he can?
Clingan was kinda quiet with 4-4-2, but blocked FIVE shots. Love that dude...

KINGS
Keegan Murray was the only starter who played, unless they end up starting Achiuwa. Nique Clifford shot 0-11 from the floor (oof).
Jonathan Mogbo went for 15 and 10 off the bench. We've seen him pop before with minutes, so keep an eye out. Rookie Alex Karaban had a solid 8-8-3 line with two threes, one block, and one steal. Deep leagues and dynasty peeps, take note.

WARRIORS
The starters played with Charles Bassey at center, while Draymond and Horford sat out. Bassey went 8-12 with 3 blocks, and I am officially acknowledging that he can't be written off entirely.
Yaxel was great (17-5-4) again, but tweaked his ankle. He said it's not bad...let's hope!
Gui Santos started again, and I think he's going to start opening night. He's def worth a pick late in drafts.

LAKERS
Austin Reaves (28-4-7) is HIM! Luka was out, so AR balled out, and Walker Kessler was great (11-9, with two stocks) in just 15 minutes. I'm aggressively targeting both of them in all formats.
Mamu had 10-7-2 with two threes off the bench. He should be rostered in standard leagues.

THUNDER
OKC played some of their important guys, notably Jalen W (16-4-3), SGA, Cason Wallace, and Hartenstein. 
Jared McCain had 20 points off the bench and took 12 threes. Ajay Mitchell was out, but holy shit, that dude is firing away shots; don't sleep on him entirely.

PACERS
Tyrese Haliburton looks phenomenal, going for 24 points on 9-14 from the floor. 
Zubac was fantastic, going 13-13-5 with three steals. The two of them are sympatico already; I am bumping them both up a bit.
Siakam went 2-for-11 shooting with just 6 points. He's an easy fade for me. Zubac is going to steal boards, Hali is going to steal points and assists, and I won't be surprised if he has his worst overall season in Indiana.

CAVS
Not much new here. The starting five played about 60% of their normal minutes, and both Peyton Watson and Jarrett Allen showed why they're probably both being overdrafted.
Jaylon Tyson and Super Mario Hezonja were both great off the bench again, while rookie Meleek Thomas had 16 points in 12 minutes. I don't think Thomas plays over Craig Porter Jr. to start the year, but he's too good to ride the pine all season either.

MAGIC
We finally saw the projected starting five, and they worked Cleveland over. Paolo looks rejuvenated (24-8-3), and Franz Wagner (a unicorn!) was awesome (20-4-8), too.
Jase Richardson and Tristan da Silva played well off the bench, leading the reserves in minutes (Anthony Black was out). Neither is probably rosterable in standard leagues, but will be streamer-worthy when Jalen Suggs is inevitably hurt.

posts.author: Andrew Weatherman
posts.text:
Little basketball analytics rant.

I’ve been seeing more and more people on my timeline use points-per-possession (“PPP”) when talking about actions (and even shooting?). Maybe my timeline has just gotten more college basketball-heavy, but PPP has quietly become a catch-all stat, and it’s getting stretched way past what it measures.

PPP is a team efficiency number. It’s great for game- or season-long efficiency, and it’s usually what you’re seeing reported as offensive/defensive rating.

When we’re measuring action-level events (picks, drives, isolations, etc.), we want points-per-chance (“PPC”). A chance splits possessions into distinct scoring opportunities, broken up by offensive rebounds and dead balls.

Say you run a pindown and the pass gets deflected out of bounds. From the side-out, you run something else and score two. The pindown produced zero points, but PPP credits it with two because you scored on the same possession. PPC gives it zero.

If you want to be more precise, you can attribute putback points to the chance that created the miss. Then there’s the concept of direct chances (and true points/shot for shooting!), but this post is already long enough.

Some additional thoughts on the Oct. 8th preseason games:

Sixers vs Nets

Sixers

- The big story in this one was not LeBron's or Brown's debut. It was how bad Embiid looked. In 24 minutes, he put up 6/3/8. That 8 is not his assists. That 8 is his turnovers. He looked every bit as bad as that stat line suggests. That video of him passing on an oop and showing off what looked like a 2-inch vert was pretty shocking as well. That being said...Embiid always looks like hot garbage in the preseason. He's one of those guys who plays himself into shape. He could be cooked, but I don't think tonight tells us that. Unfortunately, we probably won't know until November if he still has much left in the tank. I'm not drafting him anywhere close to his ADP in H2H leagues. Even in Roto, I would want him at a discount. He's still not a great pick in his range in Roto if he gives us 50 games of top-25 numbers. For now, I'm assuming he's still very good on offense but pretty washed on defense. That's mostly going off what we saw last year. That's a bigger problem for the Sixers than his fantasy value.
- LeBron only took one shot but went to the line 8 times. That worked out to a 15.3% usage rate, which is role player-level. It's not going to be that low, but I would be very surprised if he hit 20 PPG this year. The dimes should go up, though. He's another Sixer I'm staying far, far away from at his ADP. I think he's more of a top-60 per-game player this year in nine-cat. He's probably missing 20+ games. You can't take that in the fourth.
- Maxey and Brown both looked sharp. They will be a little inconsistent due to Embiid and James being in and out of the lineup, but I think their final numbers will justify where they are being drafted. I'm good with Maxey in the middle of the first. I'm good with Brown toward the end of the fourth in 12-teamers.
- Edgecombe was solid too. I'm not really shying away from him either. His threes, steals, and minutes give him a pretty solid floor, and there's a good chance that he spends a good chunk of the year as the team's third option.

Nets

- No Sharpe tonight, so Wagner got the start. He could be a deep league guy if Sharpe goes down at some point.
- No MPJ either, so Clowney started. Zero interest there. He's just not very good, and his game isn't as category league-friendly as it is made out to be. He's not a high-upside guy, even in a big role.
- Ellis is going to start until Brown is back. He's draftable in 14-team leagues and is a nice Week 1 stream in shallower settings. Brown will probably be somewhat limited early.
- Demin had 13 on 13 shots, but I would argue this was an encouraging night because he took 10 shots inside the arc. He only went 4 for 10 on those shots, but for Demin, that is a big improvement. He was one of the worst players in the league inside the arc last year. He played 25 MPG and only took two shots per night from two. I'm not expecting any miracles, but it is nice to see him expand his game, as it gives him a better shot at being more than a punt FG%-only player. That's really the only build I'm targeting him in, but I think as the Nets' likely third option, he could improve enough over the course of the season to be more than that.
- Next to Ellis, Minott is the most interesting of the Nets' likely bench options, but I'm not using a pick on him. Bad players with fantasy-friendly games are usually a trap. We watch and pick him up if he starts to look good.

Heat vs Pelicans

 Heat

- Giannis looked really good again. He's absolutely fine at 5 in H2H leagues if you are comfortable punting FT%. If you are not, sign up for EFB and learn how to do it properly. It requires a very specific approach.
- Wiggins had 13 in 15 minutes. He's being slept on this year. He was great last season. His line being Roto-ish causes him to be underrated. Glue guys are useful too.
- Mitchell is just a dimes streamer. Don't draft him outside of deep leagues.
- Portis is going to be a must-roster at points this year. We just don't know when. He's not a bad Roto or points league flier. He's draftable in deeper H2H leagues too.

Pelicans

- Herb came off the bench tonight, so maybe he's not locked in as a starter. Mathurin started for him, which is unfortunate. We want Bey in that spot. Mathurin is nothing, even if he starts.
- Murray sat, so Fears started and didn't do much. He's only going to be worth considering before the final round if he starts.
- Bey didn't start, but he played all 17 of his minutes in the first half. He needs to be watched very closely. If he's an opening night starter, he will be someone to run to if he goes undrafted in your league.
- Queen had a rough game off the bench. Five turnovers in 16 minutes. High-upside, but he's going to need a Zion injury. He's a much better pick in Roto than in H2H since you can wait out Zion.
- Missi is a nice late-round big man target for big man builds like punt FT% and punt threes. He looks pretty likely to start. 

Lakers vs. Kings

Lakers

- Reaves debuted and had a rough shooting night. However, he did have 8 dimes to Luka's 3. He was probably just easing himself in. I would expect him to be more aggressive next time out. He's fine anywhere in the second. 
- Luka is 17/18 from the line this preseason. Don't read into that at all. Luka figured out how to shoot free throws! is always an early-season storyline, and then he ends up shooting 78%.
- Grimes had 12 points on 8 shots in 29 minutes. I think he'll be worth a roster spot in 14-team leagues. In 12-team leagues, it's pretty iffy. He's just a late-round flier there in cat and points leagues.

Kings

- Acuff couldn't build off his impressive opener. He scored 12 on 4/15 shooting, only had 1 dime, and had three turnovers. The lone positive was that he had two steals. That's going to be a big swing category for him. He managed just 0.8 SPG in 35 MPG at Arkansas. It's hard for point guards (and especially rookie point guards) to be super useful if they come with a major steals hit. Bad steals PGs have to be very good on offense to be mid-round players. College steal rate is a good predictor of NBA steal rate, so last year's number is a little scary. He's still just a flier to me.
- Raynaud had 13/10 in 24 minutes. We know he's good. He'll probably start at some point this year. We just don't know when. I don't think you can draft him in H2H because he won't play beside Sabonis, but in Roto, he's viable as a bench option.
- Still not Keegan, so Precious started and put up a big line. We know he can be useful too. He'll be someone to keep an eye on all year.
- Hunter had 3 points in 18 minutes on 1-6 shooting. No bueno. I'd draft him in 16-team leagues. Probably not in 14-teamers.

posts.author: Adam Stock
posts.text:
Some thoughts on the Oct. 8 preseason games:

Spurs vs Hawks

Spurs

- Harper starting is getting all the hype, which is understandable, but with Tobias and Fox out, I don't know how much we can read into it. However, what is definitely notable and exciting about Harper's night is the threes. 3/5 from deep in just 19 minutes. It's nice that they went in, but that would be exciting even if he was 1/5. If Harper is going to be a 1.5+ 3PG player this year, that ups his ceiling a round or two. If he keeps taking them over the rest of the preseason, I would be comfortable going a little above his current ADP. We should keep an eye on his FT% too this preseason. We need him to make a jump there. His steal rate is a big question mark as well. It was surprisingly mediocre last year after being pretty solid at Rutgers. College steal rate is usually a good predictor of NBA steal rate, so last year's performance was unexpected. His college steal rate suggests he has some upside in the category.
- Wemby was a bit quiet, but that doesn't mean much. We should pay very little attention to how stars play in preseason unless they are coming off a big injury or are in a new role.
- I'm not interested in Vassell in 12-team leagues. I don't think he's even all that interesting in 14-team leagues either. He's done as a quality fantasy option as long as he's in SA.

Hawks

- Johnson rested tonight, which led to Wiggins starting at the four. He put up a pretty nice line in 24 minutes, but he's just a watch list guy for now, even in deep leagues. The Hawks' backup four minutes are up for grabs, but it's a position that will only matter if Johnson goes down. Which could happen. He's been somewhat fragile up to this point.
- Daniels took 16 shots in 21 minutes. If he does that in a JJ game, that would be interesting, but for now, I would assume he'll be the low-usage guy he's always been.

Wizards vs Knicks

Wizards

- AD's debut for the Wizards went very well. He looked like his usual self. He's pretty tempting in round 2. I would definitely think about it. I like him more than most of the injury-prone guys because when healthy, he can help the teams built around the later first-round picks compete with teams built around the big boys. I'd stay away if I landed one of the top four. You have a championship ceiling in that scenario. You don't need to take a major swing. If your first-round pick is someone like Ant or Johnson, you do need to take some swings at some point. 
- Dybantsa had four steals in 23 minutes. He had a bad steal rate in college, so for now I would assume this was a fluke performance. He's just a final-round flier to me in both category and points leagues.
- Kyshawn started and looked pretty good. 12/7/5 with a block and two threes in 22 minutes. It's hard to see how he picks up enough usage to be more than a back-end player, but I would still draft him. I like the talent, and his game is fantasy-friendly. 
- Ayton started for Sarr, who is expected to be back for the opener. We don't need to draft him anywhere, but Ayton will be a grab whenever one of the starting bigs is out, which could be a fair amount. 

Knicks

- All five Knicks starters played, and as usual nothing too interesting happened. Wake me up when someone gets hurt. From a fantasy standpoint, teams don't get any more straightforward than NY.

Celtics vs. Cavaliers

Celtics

- The Celtics rested their starters and a couple of their top bench guys, so there is nothing to see here. 

Cavaliers

- Everyone but Harden played for the Cavs. Tyson filled in for Harden. That's a good piece of info to file away for later. He played quite well in limited minutes. I'd draft him in 16-team leagues for sure. In 14, he's viable as a flier too. Good player with a fantasy-friendly game. He's just blocked, for now.
- Watson had 7/4/4 with two blocks in 17 minutes. I don't think we can read too much into his lines until we see him with all four stars healthy.

NBA Preseason Wednesday Night Notes

The only real situation I'm monitoring in Phoenix is Oso vs. Maluach for center minutes. Oso played 17 and started, going 8-2-2 with a steal. Maluach played 25 min off the bench, finishing with 8-7-4, no threes or blocks.  

I'm resetting expectations for Maluach a bit, but he's still the guy to roster. Oso just doesn't do much with his minutes and will always be the fifth option, no matter who he's out there with.

For the Bulls, Caleb Wilson (6-16) and Matas Buzelis (6-15) were wildly inefficient, combining to shoot 0-10 from three. It's good to see the volume there, and the shooting is bound to be better. Matas had 2 steals and 2 blocks. Still love him as a breakout, and Wilson oozes upside, but is going to have some rough nights, as all rookies do.

OKC studs looked great, and I like J-Dub for a bounceback year. Cason Wallace is a nice late-round value for steals as well. 

Aday Mara went nuts and looks tremendous, but he's just not going to play this year much unless Chet or Hartenstein are out. 

Jared McCain got up 11 shots in 16 minutes; he's still on my radar even though Ajay Mitchell is the bench guy we really want and a spot starter on nights that OKC starters are rested or hurt.

Kel'el Ware started at the four alongside Turner and had a very nice line of 18-12 with a block. Turner, FWIW, had 19-5 with 3 stocks and is a potential value late in drafts, too. 

Will they use this lineup in the regular season? They should, but even if Ware comes off the bench, he's still a breakout candidate and a target in the middle rounds.

Brayden Burries went 16-5-1 with 2 steals and is a guy I love in dynasty, though I'm not sure he'll have a large role this year unless Milwaukee moves a guard ahead of him.

The Magic starters didn't play much, other than Jase Richardson, who started for Suggs. Tristan da Silva put up a 19-5-2 line but on 6-for-16 shooting. He was solid as a fill-in last season, but isn't really draftable with Orlando at full strength.

Ty Jerome scored 17 points on 14 shots in 19 minutes. He's still a value late in drafts, but for how long? Feels like he's being touted EVERYWHERE. 

Boozer was solid with 16-6-2, while GG Jackson went off for 15 points in 13 minutes off the bench. He's a guy to keep an eye on for deep leagues if he sticks in the rotation for around 20 minutes a night. 

Memphis is going to be a mess, though. With 15 guys they want to play and develop, so other than Jerome, Coward, Edey, and Boozer, it's incredibly tough to project who else gets minutes.

I was happy to see Jaden McDaniels aggressive on offense, scoring 16 points and knocking down four threes. I am higher on him than most.

Kuminga stunk (and I already tweeted this last night) is not someone you need to draft in standard leagues.

The Pacers didn't play their starters much, but Aaron Nesmith had a nice game with 19 points and 4 threes. He struggled last year without Hali, but could carve out enough value to be rosterable in 12-teamers this year.

Jay Huff was awesome, too, going 16-4-2 with two stocks, and is a deep league UNICORN that shouldn't be slept on.

The Warriors played pretty much no one from their projected regular season projected rotation, so I don't care much about Dalen Terry's 23 points or Brandon Williams or Charles Bassey, yada yada

Even with Dame and Morant in the lineup, Deni Avdija put up 23 points for Portland. He and Clingan are the only early/middle round targets on this team. Dame is okay late, Morant is not someone I'm touching in 9-cat, and I've even lost my zeal for Camara after another season last year where he was just "okay." 

This rotation is also going to be a mess, but perhaps Jrue Holiday or Robert Williams will play enough for some deep league value.

NBA preseason opens up tomorrow with the Heat taking on my Raptors. I’m very high on Toronto this season with Kawhi returning. Key driver will be the continued development of Scottie Barnes, he displayed all-world potential in that 1st round matchup vs the Cavs, he dominated his matchup against Evan Mobley and was the best player on the floor in that series. 

Raptors are around +2200 to win the title now after hovering around +4500 when the Leonard Clippers trade was uncertain in the summer. The east will be a gauntlet this year, but they have a legit chance at breaking through. I think they’ll eventually have the best defense in the east. Look out for CMB, Ja’Kobe Walter & Jamal Shead, all of whom made legit strides last season. 

Miami is a very interesting team. Currently around +3500 to win the title. Surrounding Giannis with players that can stretch the floor consistently has been a successful recipe for years. Adding Klay Thompson & Tim Hardaway Jr. should pay off. 

Trading Kel’el Ware was disappointing, he’s a very promising young talent, but they wanted to accelerate their competitive timeline & getting Bobby Portis back in the Giannis trade was big.

I’m expecting a big leap from Pelle Larsson this season, a player that exceeded his contract value by a significant margin last season. 

This Heat team can make some noise this season in a crowded eastern conference. Erik Spoelstra should be able to manage Giannis effectively.

I don’t think Kawhi will play in the preseason opener tomorrow, but Giannis should start. The journey begins.
